A Chinese automatic rifle, calibre 7.62 millimetres; an automatic sniper rifle; again an automatic rifle with 840 bullets; 8 automatic rifle rounds; 19 hand-held grenades with fuses made in China; a pistol Walter, of the make Walter; a Browning pistol, calibre 7.62 millimetres; a large quantity of ammunition; a hunting knife; a pair of military binoculars; military uniforms; two hand-held radio stations; two gas masks with filters; one military belt, I don't know what the English word would be; a military sketch in Albanian showing how automatic weapons were to be fired; several maps showing the borders of their so-called Republic of Kosovo; two maps of the town of Pristina; several books of the military forces of Albania; medical supplies; wigs; caps; tape recorders; and materials prepared for the issuing of a newspaper called "Qerime" [phoen]; various books and magazines; military booklets with the name of Fatmir Gasi; personal identity cards belonging to Saban Seman [phoen], Naser Musali [phoen]; one of them was from Pristina, the other from Podujevo, another man from Pristina; a military booklet in the name of Fatmir Gasi from Pristina and his health insurance booklet. Their addresses were in other places, but they had rented this flat in order to conduct their activities in it. The body of Isef Hajdari was found in the yard of this house, and next to him, a pistol, Browning pistol, a 7.65 calibre, and a round of 8 bullets were found next to his body, as well as two boxes of ammunition, one containing 25 bullets and the other 17. He was injured in the head, and his body was transferred to the forensic institute for an autopsy. In this attack, policemen Svetislav Petrovic was injured who was born in 1968, and he received severe injuries, an entry wound to the right buttock and superficial injuries. He was transferred to the surgery in Pristina for medical assistance. The crime scene was photographed, a sketch was made, and the photo footage was taken with a video camera which actually make up part of this on-site investigation report. As no other individuals were found in this house except for the body, it is -- it was assumed that one of those who fired the shots was Isuf Hajdari, but the other perpetrators were not discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I tender this exhibit into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00865.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, can we pause to think what we are doing. We have now been through ten reports out of what I anticipate will be a total of some 30. We have a summary of each one of those in the statement of Mrs. Marinkovic, and we will have exhibited the report. I'm not sure how strong her voice is, but if she's going to have to virtually read a further 20 of these reports, it's going to be a big strain on her, and it's going to take us a great deal of time when we will have them all to read. It occurs to me that it may be possible to be much quicker in dealing with these and spare the task of having to read everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I definitely agree with you, Your Honours. I will switch in Serbian now. [Interpretation] And I will ask Mrs. Marinkovic, the witness, to comment on the next documents, and could she just confirm whether she has actually drafted that report. And then we won't go in detail into the report, so that I believe that from now on we will be able to proceed with greater speed. And I appreciate your comments, Your Honours. The next Defence case is D007-2660.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That's under tab 12 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This on-site investigation report was filed under number Kri 123/98 and was compiled on the 8th of August, 1998. I compiled the document and signed it. I conducted the investigation. And this relates to an event in Bresje village, Kosovo Polje municipality, where an explosive device was tossed into the yard of the Bogujevci family. It states in the report what was found and the established circumstances, both with regards to the damage and the crime. There were no casualties. This involved the victims, an Albanian family which had been warned by the KLA --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That will suffice, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00866.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next exhibit is D007-2664. Could we please see it on the monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, Witness, Mrs. Marinkovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, this is 2660. I apologise. That was the one we've just discussed, so now we want 2664. Bear with me. The next exhibit on the Defence 65 ter list is 2664. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: So in your binder, you can find that under tab 13. Could you tell us briefly something about this incident.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is another on-site investigation report conducted by me as investigating judge together with the an investigating team. The investigation was conducted on the 27th of August, 1998 in, Dragodan where an explosive device was tossed into a yard of the -- actually, the courtyard of the American information centre. There were no casualties, but there was damage to the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Where was this building?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The building was in Dragodan settlement which is an urban neighbourhood, and it is predominantly an Albanian settlement or neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What about the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The perpetrators were not discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00867.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next exhibit is D007-2668.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, that's under tab 14. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is an on-site investigation compiled by me on the 11th of September, 1998, under Kri number 156/98. I signed this form and the investigation was conducted in Kosare village, Urosevac municipality. After an attack on employees of the Stimlje revenue administration on which occasion an employee of the revenue administration, Mihajlovic, Sinisa from Stimlje was killed. The perpetrators were never discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00868.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next exhibit is D007-2565 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: And in your binder, Mrs. Marinkovic, that's under tab 15.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is an on-site investigation report. Here we don't have a Kri number, but rather a Kio number, 119/98. It was compiled on the 31st of June -- on the 30th of June, 1998, in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just pause for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we have an error in the transcript regarding the number of the exhibit. The number -- the correct number should be D008-5256. 5256. [In English] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go on. This is the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I mentioned that this was not a Kri number because that number would mean that it was an on-site investigation before the investigation was actually initiated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please pause for a moment here. This is one example where we want to pause for minute to describe the difference. When testify we have the Kri and Kio, could you describe what the distinctions of these numbers are?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when an official file is filed under a Kri number, this is a case file where on-site investigation reports are filed and where an investigation has actually not been initiated yet. So this is still in the phase of the investigative measures, the preliminary investigative measures. In other words, an on-site investigation was conducted, perhaps an autopsy if that was the case. And once a perpetrator is found, these files would then be joined to the Kio files where then an investigation would be conducted. In Pristina we had Kri and Kio numbers. We did not use Ki numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now please discuss this one.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is a Kio number, and it was filed as such because one of the accused, Iljber Topali, who was accused in the case Kio 119/98, which I conducted on the grounds that a criminal organisation was established in order to engage in enemy activity. So I conducted this, and one of the accused was brought into my office. And when his handcuffs were taken off, instead of sitting down, he jumped over my desk, dashed past me, and rushed out of my office, and then he started running down the street where the district court was. The guards who escorted him ran after him, and in this rush to catch him, one of the guards shot at him and injured him, injured him in the back. He fell down, and then we went to the crime scene to conduct an on-site investigation. He was still alive, and I immediately ordered that he be transferred to the hospital, after which he was transferred from the Pristina hospital to Belgrade for treatment. He was treated there, and postoperative rehabilitation was conducted in the Belgrade hospital. And in this period I went to see him together with a deputy public prosecutor, his defence counsel, and an interpreter. We visited him at the hospital where I conducted an interview with him, so that when he recovered an indictment was raised against him, and when the court -- when the proceedings, the court proceedings began, he attended proceedings, he was in good health, and he was able to attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, could I now please tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00869.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretaiton] I would now appreciate seeing Exhibit D007-2672.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder that's under tab 16, Mrs. Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you briefly comment on this. First of all, are you the drafter of this document or, rather, of this report?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is an on-site investigation report drafted by me, Kri number 188/98, regarding an incident on the 3rd of November, 1998, in Gracko village, Lipljan municipality, where a terrorist attack was -- following a terrorist attack on Fehmi Sopa family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: And the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: The perpetrators were not discovered. But I would like to mention here that in addition to finding shells on the crime scene, we also found a camouflage greyish green beret, and we knew that such berets were actually berets used by members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D00870.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D007-2676.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, Mrs. Marinkovic, that's under tab 18.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Regarding this event, described in the on-site investigation report before us under number Kri 201/98, of 9 November, 1998, and compiled in Malisevo village on site where a terrorist attack had been conducted on a police building, and on this day, we conducted an investigation and found the bodies of the SUP Pristina policeman who had been murdered, Vujosevic, Ilija; and Dejan Djatlov. I would like to add when speaking of this incident that these two policemen had previously been abducted while they were transporting food on a truck for police station from Pristina to Malisevo, and for seven days no one knew where they were. We had some indications that there was a terrorist group, KLA terrorist group, a large stronghold in Malisevo, and that the KLA staff was in Malisevo. And when they were getting ready to go to investigate this incident on site, we were told by the policemen that it was risky to go and conduct an on-site investigation there. The president of the court and the district prosecutor was informed of this, and I was summoned as the investigating judge on duty and the deputy prosecutor. Everyone agreed that it was too risky, that it wasn't secure, and that they were not to go on site to conduct an on-site investigation. The prosecutor decided not to go, but knowing that the bodies of these two policemen had been found on site, and we were told by the police officers who attended the crime scene that their bodies had been massacred --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mutilated, interpreters correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... I decided as an investigating judge to go and conduct an on-site investigation which I was authorised to do even without the presence of the public prosecutor or, rather, his deputy, but I asked the police to just send a stronger security detail to accompany me. And that is why it says here that the crime scene was secured by special units of the republican MUP. When I arrived on the crime scene and when I saw what had been done to those two bodies, it was a horrible site. It was a catastrophe. These people were tortured, then they were mutilated, and their bodies thrown out on to the street. We conducted an on-site investigation and took the bodies in order to conduct an autopsy on them. And as we started back we drew fire from all sides, and there was so much shooting that we barely managed to pull out of there alive. When I returned to court I was criticised both by the president of the court and the prosecutor for going there and not actually minding what they told me; however, when I returned, I was very happy that I did actually go to this crime scene and that we brought the bodies back so they wouldn't be pulled away by dogs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, may I tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00871.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this is the right moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. We will have the second break now. We resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Could we please see document D007-2680 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That's tab 18 in your binder, madam. Please go ahead, be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is also an official document, an on-site investigation report filed under number Kri 203/98. It's dated 11 November, 1998. On that day I, as investigating judge, with the other members of the on-site investigation team conducted the on-site investigation at Glogovac since a terrorist attack was carried out on the premises of the Glogovac Internal Affairs and other facilities. We stated here what we found there, what the material damage was, the evidence such as cartridges at several locations, and that there was protracted shooting from various directions and that large material damage was inflicted to buildings. Police officers, Slavko Amidzic and Srdjan Stevanovic were wounded. Significant material damage was done to the house of the family of Xhafer Xhory [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were the perpetrators found?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00872.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document D007-2687.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, that's tab 19, madam.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is also an on-site investigation report that I drew up about an incident that happened on the 18th of December, 1998, at Careva Cesma nearby Glogovac where the body of Zvonko Bojanic from Velika Slatina was discovered. I wish to say that Zvonko Bojanic was abducted by KLA members two days prior to that. He was kidnapped from his house where his family were present. His whereabouts were unknown until his body was found on the road. It was mutilated. A vehicle was run over him, and considering the agreement between the federal government and the OSCE -- or, rather, pursuant to that agreement, the OSCE staff were also present. They observed and asked questions when they didn't understand something.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Marinkovic, this document, Defence document, is important to all of us because this is the first time the presence of OSCE members is recorded. How were they informed? How did they know that something happened? So please explain to us how that co-operation worked in practical terms.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was in November 1998 that the agreement was made between the federal government and the OSCE, and we had a good co-operation, they and I. They were informed by the duty service of the Pristina SUP, the secretariat was duty-bound to inform them of incidents, and that an investigating judge would go to the site with a team, and they had the right to be present if they wished. But they were not allowed to take active part in the investigation activities. They could take notes the way they considered appropriate, and during the investigation sometimes they would ask questions when they didn't understand something or when they wanted additional clarification, and we gave them such information, but that didn't amount to interfering with the work of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That will do. I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00873.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see document D007-2719.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That's tab 20 in your binder, madam. We can see that the same place is mentioned, namely the Careva Cesma location.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Give us a brief account.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: On this day an on-site investigation was conducted because at the same place, Careva Cesma, the body of an unknown male was discovered. The body was mutilated, and it bore traces of torture. The body was transferred to the forensic medicine ward for identification and autopsy. It was established that it was Bratislava Sekic who had come from Belgrade to visit his family. He was -- he stayed at the Grand Hotel in Pristina due to a frequent terrorist attacks, and we learned that on the following morning he took a taxi to Urosevac, but that was the last that was seen of him until the body was discovered. And hereto representatives of the OSCE were present during the on-site investigation. The names of all persons present are stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00874.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document that we'd like to see on the screen is D007-0674.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Now we are going into 1999. This is -- we are showing this really by way of illustration. We will soon pass over to different topics. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This document is filed under Kri 29/99. It's an on-site investigation report drafted by me about an incident that happened on the 1st of February, 1999, in the village of Gornje Godance in the Stimlje municipality when a terrorist attack was carried out on the family of Jetulah Zumeri. They said that on that day KLA members in black clothes, black uniforms armed with automatic rifles entered their house. Their intention was to take a man with them. The family resisted that, but in the process two persons were wounded. The names of those wounded and their injuries are stated in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, too, OSCE representatives were present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00875.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is D007-2727. Can we please see it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is an on-site investigation report drafted by me following a terrorist attack in Pristina, in down-town Pristina. The Ardido i Anda bar was attacked on the 5th of February, 1999. The owner of that bar was Gzim Kastrati. The on-site investigation was conducted in the presence of OCE representatives, their were people wounded, their names are mentioned in the report, damage was done to the bar, and the evidence found is also listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Why was this bar attacked?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: In early 1999, some Albanians who wanted to work and make a living rented business facilities owned by Serbs. This was the Dardanija neighbourhood where both Albanians and Serbs lived. But some Serbs also owned business space, but they were unable to engage in their own business activity there, so they rented it out to Albanians. But these Albanians were punished because they co-operated with Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00876.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next Defence document is D007-0678. Can we see it on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This is tab 23 in your binder, madam. Is the situation here similar?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's an on-site investigation report. I conducted that investigation on the 6th of February, 1999, in Pristina. In Vidovdanska Street where a terrorist attack was carried out close to Mala Pijaca, where Albanians were harmed because they had their shops there. The investigation was conducted in the presence of OSCE members. Some people were killed in the incident. A girl born in the 1981 was killed and two men. All Albanians. One was born in 1947, and the other in 1978.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00877.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next Defence document is D007-2711. Could we please see it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Marinkovic, that's tab 24 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: In this document there's an on-site investigation report that was conducted on 22 February, 1999, in the village of Pali Vodenica in the Kacanik municipality, following a terrorist attack on the Ljoki family, when Gafur and Driton Ljoki were killed, father and son. They were shot from fire-arms by KLA members who wore black camouflage uniforms. This on-site investigation was also conducted in the presence of OSCE representatives for the Kacanik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00878.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next Defence document is D007-2707.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That is tab 25 in your binder, madam. Could we please see it on our screen.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This document that we see is also an official on site investigation report drafted by me. It's filed as Kri 51/99. It's dated 27 February, 1999. Following a terrorist attack on an official police vehicle which was ambushed nearby Krivovo in the Slatina municipality -- or, rather, the Kosovo Polje municipality close to Slatina, in this attack policemen were killed. Milorad Mitic born in 1966 was killed, and some persons were wounded. Milorad Petronijovic [phoen] and Ljubisa Denic. The on-site investigation was conducted in the presence of OSCE representatives from Glogovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00879.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next Defence document is D007-2715. That is tab 26 in your binder, madam. Could we please see it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is an on-site investigation report. The number is Kri 53/99, compiled on the 28th February, 1999. I compiled it as the investigating judge, and it concerns an event in the village of Gajre, Kacanik municipality, when a terrorist attack on a police patrol was mounted, and the police patrol was from the Kacanik police station. In this terrorist attack, the commander of the Kacanik police station was killed; his name was Bogoljub Staletovic. And policemen, Slobodan Jankovic, Zoran Djuric, Sladjan Jovanovic, and Djordje Milosavljevic were seriously injured. A member of the terrorist gang was found on-site. He was the one who fired shots at this police patrol from an ambush. He actually launched a shell from a hand-held launcher made in Russia. We found this weapon and other weapons as well as a uniform and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did he have anything else with him, a back-pack or something like that?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had a back-pack containing civilian clothing with him. We already knew that this was their method of operating. After carrying out a terrorist attack, they would change into civilian clothes, discard their military uniform with KLA insignia, and mix in with the local population, so as not to be discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00880.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is D007-2691.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder it's tab 27, Mrs. Marinkovic. Can we please have it up on the screen. And just give us a brief comments on it.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is an on-site investigation report compiled on the 21st of March, 1999, in the village of Poklek, Glogovac municipality, concerning a terrorist and sabotage attack in front of the railway crossing on the bridge over the Drenica river at the entrance to Glogovac. This bridge was regularly used by police vehicles and also by citizens passing through from Pristina towards Glogovac. The bridge was damaged so as to be out of use for awhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00881.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is D007-0683.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, it's number 28, Mrs. Marinkovic. May it be up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This on-site investigation report was compiled by myself as investigating judge concerning an event which took place on the 21st of March, 1999, in Pristina in Miladina Popovica Street, which is in an urban area, a built-up area in Pristina, when fire was opened from an ambush on policemen in a patrol vehicle passing down the street. In this terrorist attack, Aleksandar Milojekovic, Dejan Hepkovic [phoen], and Milivoj Nicic [phoen] sustained fatal injuries, as did Vladimir Jevtic. Policemen Nedzad Osmani was wounded, while policemen Zeljko Mitrovic remained uninjured.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were the perpetrators found?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00882.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is D007-2699.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder it's number 29, Mrs. Marinkovic. Please comment on it briefly.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is another on-site investigation report which I compiled as the investigating judge. I carried out the on-site investigation with my team on the 22nd of March, 1999, in Njegoseva Street in connection with a terrorist attack on the Koha coffee bar owned by Ramiz Balja from Pristina. Arinit Keljmendi born in 1969 was seriously injured, and he died of his injures in the insensitive care unit of the Pristina Surgical Clinic. Jasmina Jaha was also seriously injured, as was Agrib Balja. The attack was mounted for the same reasons that I mentioned before. These were catering establishment owned by Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. May this be admitted into evidence, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00883.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D007-2655. 2695. I do apologise, 2695.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, it's 30, madam.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Please comment on this briefly.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is another on-site investigation report. I carried out the investigation on the 22nd of March, 1999, in Pristina. A terrorist attack was mounted in the Medik coffee bar owned by Agron Ljumezi from Pristina. Fire was opened on this coffee bar from an automatic weapon, spent cartridges were found on site. And Leonida Ljutoli, born in 1977, died. Vedat Bahtiri was injured and given medical assistance in the surgical centre in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the last incident that took place before the air-strikes. May it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00884.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is D007-0727.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: It's number 31 in your binder, madam. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: I drew up this on-site investigation report and the 20th of April, 1999, regarding damaged facilities in Grmija, the post office communications building and the Executive Council building. These buildings were damaged in connection with NATO bombs, because they were hit in the morning by NATO bombs. Both buildings were completely destroyed, and in the rubble we found the body of an employee of the Executive Council. His name was Branko Gudic, he was born in 1944.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time were there still OSCE observers there?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, immediately before the air-strikes began they had left Pristina and were now in Skopje in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00885.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, D007-0668.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, it's number 32. Could we have it up on the screen, please, and could you comment on it briefly.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: This is an on-site investigation report which I compiled as the investigating judge when the state of war had already been declared and NATO air-strikes started. I compiled this on the 11th of May, 1999, when I contacted an on-site investigation in Staro Gracko, Lipljan municipality, where three people were killed by NATO aircraft and three suffered serious injuries. Many cluster bombs had been launched there, family homes were damaged. There were no military facilities in the vicinity, and we found a large quantity of cluster bombs in the vicinity which we did not dare touch because we didn't know which of them had been activated and which not. All this is recorded here and photographs are attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00886.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may we have D011-4543 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: It's number 33 in your binder. This is an interesting document on which we will dwell a little. Can you explain first of all, whether you compiled this document?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, before I begin commenting on this document, in connection with these on-site investigation reports that we have been looking at, in each one the data is recorded and also the investigating judge in compliance with the law, whenever carrying out an on-site investigation, had to check that the place had been secured by the police, and that was the same for every on-site investigation. So the police would secure the site, they would mark the site, and guard it so as to avoid evidence and traces being lost. When an on-site investigation is carried out, depending on the security situation, the police also have to be present. But the number of policemen and whether only ordinary police officers would be there or the commander of the station or the chief, that would all depend on the security situation. And I'm saying this because in each of these reports, there is a list of who was present from the police, and the police were the only persons authorised to secure the site. But they were not allowed to interfere with the work of the investigating judge and the investigating team from the court who are carrying out the on-site investigation. I wanted to explain this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what can we say about the document on the screen? In your binder it's number 33. And the document is entitled "Review of cases in which I as investigating judge conducted investigations..."

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: In this document as a practicing judge, I wanted to make it easier to facilitate the work of this Tribunal, so I compiled a review of cases in which I had conducted investigations. And after my investigation, the prosecutor raised an indictment, trials were conducted, verdicts reached, and appeals filed. I showed here only some of the cases where I carried out the investigations for the crime of conspiring to engage in hostile activities and the terrorism. I made an overview as to the target, whether the persons targeted were civilians, Albanians, and so on, whether the buildings targeted were buildings housing police stations, refugees, buildings where the families of police officers were, and in each case how many people had been killed and how many injured, to make it easier for the Chamber to look at the documents. I also made a list of how many sentences had been handed out, how many people were found guilty, how many were acquitted, what the sentences were, and this covers only part of the cases I was involved in. There were other cases I dealt with and some dealt with by my colleagues, but those I was not able to obtain. And there were also cases dealt with by other district courts in Kosovo and Metohija. So there were many, many more cases than those mentioned here in this review.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question is the following: As we have now seen, the most important investigating procedures you engaged in before and during the NATO air-strikes, as you mentioned, that you had dealt only with those cases falling within the territorial jurisdiction of the district court in Pristina and that you mentioned that there were four other district courts on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija at the time, do you have any direct or indirect knowledge that such criminal offences were also committed on the territories of other district courts?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that there were such cases in all courts, but I couldn't tell you the number of such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00887.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is a convenient moment to break off for today. Tomorrow we will be dealing with Racak, and before that we will look at some verdicts and sentences handed down by the court in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. We now adjourn. We resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. Again, a Court Officer will assist you when we retire. We adjourn to resume at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
